column1: # Schedule RC-R Part I -- Regulatory Capital.
# Two things about this schedule are easy to get wrong
# 1. THE BASEL I -> BASEL III CHANGE IS A PREFIX CHANGE. The same MDRM item codes carry
#    the same concepts on either side
#    A variable pointed at either one alone goes blank for half the panel. The base items
#    below are era-suffixed and the derived series stitch them.
# 2. THE REPORTED RATIOS CHANGE UNITS THREE TIMES (measured 2026-09-26; the earlier
#    belief that they are confidential from 2015Q1 was wrong -- they are ~98% populated
#                                     bulk files; data_call_report stores the number
#    The base rows below are era pieces of one code; the derived *_reported series
#    rescale the percent eras by 1/100 and publish FRACTIONS
#    ratios (tier1_capital / rwa). The computed ratios remain the primary series; the
#    reported ones are published for validation and for the CBLR banks that report a
#    leverage ratio but no RWA from 2020Q1.
# Part II -- the ~740-cell risk-weighted-asset grid -- is not covered.

Tier 1 leverage ratio as filed, one unit (fraction) across the source eras, BEFORE the filer unit-error correction (published so the correction is auditable): RCFD7204 (fraction; percent 2008Q4-2010Q4) else RCFA/RCOA7204 (fraction when filed by the 2014 Basel III early adopters, percent from 2015Q1).

Tier 1 leverage ratio AS REPORTED, as a FRACTION across every era (Basel I definition to 2014, Basel III after; the 2014 early adopters file Basel III). Filer unit errors are corrected: where the filed value is 30-300x (or 1/300-1/30 of) the ratio implied by the bank's own amounts (tier1_capital / assets) it is rescaled by 100; capital_ratio_unit_corrected counts the corrections in the row. See docs/schedules/RC-R-I.md.
column5: leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected.where(~((leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected.abs() >= 30 * (tier1_capital / assets).abs()) & (leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected.abs() <= 300 * (tier1_capital / assets).abs())), leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected / 100).where(~((leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected.abs() * 30 <= (tier1_capital / assets).abs()) & (leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected.abs() * 300 >= (tier1_capital / assets).abs())), leverage_ratio_reported_uncorrected * 100)
